title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after what they say was an unlawful traffic stop. On July 23, a Flock Safety camera misread the license plate of Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, reading a final digit 2 as 7 and flagging her car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Police pulled her over on Calle Duran, handcuffed her and her 12-year-old sister, and placed both in separate police cars before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked an officer to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers handcuffed the child anyway.

The sisters filed lawsuits on Jan. 3 seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was stopped in April after being mistakenly linked to an armed robbery. The city, police chief, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits are now pending in state District Court.
